## Copilot review overview ### 🔵 Needs a closer look Runtime deployment must wait until newly granted secret access is effective. **Review effort:** Balanced **Findings:** 1 · 2
Open (3) - [Script conflicts with existing Firestore database specification](#discussion_r4157677050) - [Align PR description with broker-side identity verification](#discussion_r4160831954) - [Correct the PR description secret names](#discussion_r4155127058)
Prevent Cloud Run deployment failures from IAM propagation delays `cloud/claude-code-cloud/setup.sh:162` BLOCKER — READ-NOT-DEMONSTRATED: these new secret IAM grants are consumed by the Cloud Run deployments later in the same one-shot apply, but IAM policy changes are eventually consistent (Google documents policy propagation as typically minutes). Cloud Run validates `secretAccessor` at deployment, so either deployment can transiently fail after the accounts, grants, and database have been created; the create-or-refuse preflight then prevents a clean retry. Split grant/provisioning from deployment, or add an effective-permission readiness gate before creating the runtimes, so propagation cannot strand the apply.
